nodes.label: RULINGS-R4g.md
nodes.author: M
nodes.rationale: The three rulings that close Phase 2 of PLAN-R4-PUBLICATION.md; successor to RULINGS-R4f.md.

nodes.label: The bracket result — composition seen from above
nodes.rationale: Register 334's sentence proved down the whole tower by the original-works return; it reserved number 1836, which was then spent by the §34.4 qualifier entry — so the draft takes the next free number, because a Register number is assigned at seating.

nodes.label: A Register entry's kind is inferred when untagged
nodes.rationale: kinds.py collapses a tagged entry to that single kind (if t: kinds={t[-1]}) and otherwise infers, with kinds that overlap by design — so an untagged entry whose headline carries a digit counts both a measurement and a finding. Only 105 of 1,721 seated entries carry a tag at all, so untagged is the ordinary form.

nodes.label: Register 1797 — a gap with no excision marker
nodes.rationale: 1796 and 1798 are seated and no EXCISED 1797 marker covers it, which RULING 27 — TWO REGISTERS does not allow. The staged entry seats at the next free number and the hole stays a hole: a number is not reused, and a gap with no marker is a fault a later entry reports rather than back-fills.

nodes.label: A chat transcript is a source R3 may repair from
nodes.author: M
nodes.rationale: M: 'yes, but the chat must be reviewed exhaustively because context frames the object in question; and usually they are also a lead with an attached instrument for verification.' Two conditions travel with the ruling — an exhaustive review, because a partial read can invert the finding, and the ordinary route of re-running the attached instrument rather than quoting prose.

nodes.label: Twelve Register entries asserting what a chat withdrew
nodes.rationale: 230, 314, 500, 502, 599, 602, 807, 1148, 1450, 1461, 1595, 1628 carry no WITHDRAWN/WARNING/REFUTED/SUPERSEDED marker while 1395 carries WARNING; each repair is a new appended entry citing the superseded one, owed the exhaustive review 3(a) requires.

nodes.label: The compendia close before the prose phase opens
nodes.author: M
nodes.rationale: M: 'the compendiums must be finished before the prose work, so the main volume pointers can be fixed during the prose phase.' A scheduling ruling, recorded as one.

nodes.label: The four intake drafts seat untagged
nodes.rationale: They were written with kind tags outside the Register's eight-kind vocabulary; seating new reader-facing kind names is an editorial decision M has not made, so the smaller available act is taken — the form 94 % of the Register already uses.
